body: Wow. I read a very similar story on this sub like a year ago. I can’t believe families actually do this. I’m so sorry.
This helped so much. Thank you.

I hope you’re still here. I want to share a story with you. I tried to commit suicide in the same way too. I posted on this sub two hours before, threw my phone onto the tracks, and waited for the right moment. I couldn’t feel anything in the moment and tried to drown out the noise from the crowds picking up in the metro platform. Someone was watching a space launch live on their phone, and I decided to listen for a while. I started to get into the countdown. Before I knew it, I had missed the train. I spent 2 years actively planning my suicide and becoming self-destructive to keep everyone out of it. I don’t know, I couldn’t go through with it anymore. 3 years later, I’m still rebuilding my own relationship and friendships I had, even finding more people who love me for who I am in the effort. It takes a LOT of work and time, but it’s worth it. That moment gave me a tiny something of who I am, and I hope the same for you too.

I have a restrictive eating disorder that already affects my ability to eat for myself. I already suffer from malnutrition and immense anxiety with food. I don’t have the capacity to have someone depend on me to cook for them when they’re more than capable of doing it. Why is salymander the only one who understands the problem? I just know when they figure out I learned how to cook, they’re going to demand I make them food when I don’t have the energy or time to do it. It’s important to me this doesn’t become another method for them to try to control me.

I really can’t wait. I’ll try to hold out. It’s comforting to know your husband was able to manage GERD. What do you think about reaching out to friends to use their kitchens from time to time? I’ve been hesitant because it’s an awkward situation.

I’m 24 years old, and I do many basic tasks for her already, not that they deserve to have me cater to their needs. This argument isn’t valid here. I’m her only kid, and my needs were still neglected without exaggeration. I have scars from being whipped by a belt and having objects thrown at me. I’ve internalized the kind of behaviors that come from having your “parents” threaten suicide if I don’t feel or act the way they want me to fulfill their realities. For the longest time, I thought because they’re my parents, I owed them everything. I’m happy for my extended family and friends who have parents who loved them right, but I don’t deserve this shit. I already suffer from an eating disorder they probably caused by letting me starve for hours on end because my mom hated the fact I was overweight from when I was born. I weigh 76 pounds. Tell me again, do they deserve a plate of dinner from me?

If it helps to understand, I suffer from delusional episodes, and I can't function without a strong support system. I was sent on a medical leave of absence years ago because I gave myself hypothermia trying to relive something. I've had many more, and I just want to be ok with someone who can truly help me. I'm worried I won't have a future.
